column1: # parser/spec/divergent.tsv — the LIVE parser parity-debt ledger (NUR060).
# One row per divergence: src <TAB> go <TAB> ts <TAB> justification.
# Same escaping and comment rules as parse.tsv. Every row is a real,
# currently-measured divergence: the Go spec runner must reproduce the
# `go` column and the TS runner the `ts` column on every run, the row
# count is machine-pinned in both runners, and the ratchet direction is
# shrink-toward-zero — a row leaves by being FIXED and moving to
# parse.tsv, never by deletion. The rows below are one representative per
# divergence class from the 2026-08-09 probe sweep (55 divergences across
# 2,587 sources); see parser/spec/README.md §"The current debt" and
# NUR.md §NUR060, which stays open until this ledger is empty again.

column4: trailing `=>` with no body: the Go arrowfold still folds (the input doubles as the body); the TS fold drops the paren group from the value stream entirely. A DATA-class divergence — Go matches the fold-always arrowfold grammar. (Go column re-rendered 2026-08-15: NUR059 gave the paren group a source form, so the Go side spells `(1 …)` rather than `paren([1 …])`; the DIVERGENCE is unchanged — TS still drops the group.)
the same trailing-arrow fold loss, inside a dotchain segment: Go folds the interp into a lambda group, TS keeps only the bare interp.

column3: ERR [boru/syntax_error]: empty list element: remove the leading/repeated comma (write `none` for an explicit empty value)
column4: a trailing bare colon: Go accepts and drops the empty implicit pair, TS refuses the whole source — an accept/reject split.

column2: ERR [boru/syntax_error]: empty list element: remove the leading/repeated comma (write `none` for an explicit empty value)
column4: `=>` then `,`: Go refuses the empty element, TS accepts and silently drops both trailing tokens — an accept/reject split in the opposite direction from the bare-colon row.

column4: after an unmatched `]`, Go names the offending token in the recovery diagnostic; TS reports an empty token. Same code, divergent detail and location.

column2: ERR [boru/syntax_error]: `.` member access has no receiver
column4: error-precedence: Go reports the receiverless `.`, TS the unmatched `(` — the two walks meet the faults in a different order.
Go refuses the bare `/s` modifier first (`empty word`); TS reports the unmatched `(`. Error-precedence divergence with a non-BoruError Go render.
both ports leak an internal marker type name into the message (`parser.unclosedParen` vs `UnclosedParen`) — neither render is a stable user-facing diagnostic.

an empty `${}` inside an UNTERMINATED backtick template: Go folds the empty interpolation to an empty literal, TS keeps the `${}` hole — a value-level fold divergence where both ports accept. Found by a truncation mutant of parse.tsv's `${}`-in-template row.
